questions.text: Is the testicular swelling painful or completely painless, and how long have you had it?
questions.purpose: Painless testicular swelling is a red flag for testicular malignancy; duration helps gauge urgency

questions.text: Is the swelling confined to the testicle itself and is it hard or firm to touch?
questions.purpose: A hard, firm mass within the testis strongly suggests testicular cancer

questions.text: Does the swelling transilluminate (light passes through it) when a torch is shone behind the scrotum?
questions.purpose: Transillumination is characteristic of a hydrocele (fluid-filled, benign), distinguishing it from solid malignant mass

questions.text: Have you noticed any associated back pain, abdominal mass, or enlarged lymph nodes?
questions.purpose: Back pain from para-aortic lymphadenopathy or abdominal mass may indicate metastatic testicular cancer

questions.text: Have you had fever, pain, or urinary symptoms suggesting infection?
questions.purpose: Infective orchitis or epididymo-orchitis presents with fever, pain, and urinary symptoms

questions.text: Have you had a previous undescended testicle (cryptorchidism), even if surgically corrected?
questions.purpose: Cryptorchidism is the strongest risk factor for testicular germ cell tumour

questions.text: Do you have breast tenderness or enlargement (gynaecomastia)?
questions.purpose: Gynaecomastia can occur with hCG-secreting testicular tumours (e.g. choriocarcinoma)
